Name: Maligne Lake
Description: Largest glacially-fed lake in the Canadian Rockies. Drive 48 km from Jasper on Maligne Road. Book the Spirit Island boat cruise in advance at malignelake.com — the postcard view of Jasper. Allow a full morning here.

Name: Spirit Island boat cruise
Description: 90-min guided cruise to Spirit Island — the most iconic view in Jasper, possibly in all of Canada. Book at malignelake.com well in advance. August slots sell out. This is non-negotiable if you're at Maligne Lake.

Name: Bald Hills trailhead
Description: Climbs above treeline to a panoramic aerial view of Maligne Lake and the surrounding peaks — far more dramatic than the lakeshore view. 10 km return, 490m gain. Do in the afternoon after the Spirit Island cruise for a perfect full Maligne day.

Name: Athabasca Falls
Description: High-volume whitewater through a tight limestone gorge — one of the most powerful waterfalls in the Rockies. Easy 20 min walk. 30 km south of Jasper on the Icefields Pkwy. Crowded midday — go in the late afternoon.

Name: Mt. Edith Cavell / Cavell Meadows
Description: One of the most dramatic scenes in Jasper NP. The Angel Glacier hangs directly off a 3000m north face above a milky moraine lake. Cavell Meadows loop (8 km, 380m gain) climbs through wildflower meadows with the glacier looming above the whole time. 27 km south of Jasper on Edith Cavell Road — fine for an SUV.

Name: Valley of the Five Lakes
Description: Five turquoise lakes in the forest — easy walking with excellent photography in afternoon light. 9 km loop, 100m gain. Good for a lower-energy afternoon after a big morning.

Name: Opal Hills trailhead
Description: Steep climb to alpine meadows above Maligne Lake. 8.2 km loop, 460m gain. Best for fit hikers on a clear day — excellent backup if Bald Hills is crowded.

Name: Pyramid Lake
Description: Scenic lake 7 km north of Jasper with Pyramid Mountain reflected in the water. Good easy evening option — short walk or paddling.

Name: Lake Annette
Description: Easy blue-water lake close to Jasper townsite. Low-effort recovery stop — good for a swim or a short walk.
